title: Lesson 2: Your Professional Setup

blocks.html:
Your first email to a new prospect goes out this morning. It arrives with no photo, no title and no phone number, from an address they don’t recognize. Two days later a colleague asks how the opportunity is going and you forward two emails by hand, because the conversation isn’t anywhere they can see.

Meanwhile Zoho has sent you 40 notifications about things you already know, so you’ve started ignoring them — which means the one that mattered went past you too.

None of this is a skill problem. It’s five settings. Twenty minutes now saves that friction on every email and every handover for as long as you’re here.

By the end of this lesson you’ll be able to:

  1. Configure your profile so colleagues can identify you at a glance.
  2. Verify that email tracking is live — and fix it if it isn’t — so correspondence logs itself.
  3. Set notifications and your signature so Zoho adds signal instead of noise.
  4. Set up the mobile app for the moments when you’re not at a desk.

About 20 minutes. Keep Zoho open in a second tab.

What “done properly” looks like

Unfinished setupFinished setup
Blank profile photo; colleagues see initials and a job title nobody has updated.Photo, title and phone number current. Time zone correct, so bookings land at the right hour.
Mailbox never linked, so you paste emails into notes by hand — or forget.Configuration Status Working, Sync Status Completed. Emails appear on the record without you doing anything.
Every notification on: your inbox fills with duplicates of what Zoho already shows you.Email notifications off for things you check in the CRM daily; deal changes still reach you.
Signature differs from the OneAccord standard, or is missing entirely.Standard OneAccord signature on every email sent from Zoho, with your booking link.

Work through the five sections below in order — one is not much use without the one before it.

1. Your profile

A complete profile is how colleagues recognise you when your name turns up on a record — and how clients see you if anything you send carries your details.

  • Photo: a professional headshot, not an avatar.
  • Details: name, title and phone number, all current.
  • Time zone: set correctly, or booking links and reminders misfire.

blocks.label: In Zoho CRM
blocks.instructions:
Click your profile icon (top right) → My Settings → Personal Settings. Upload your photo, check your name, title, phone and time zone, then save. Close the settings panel with the red X when you’re done.

Then, in the same menu, open Notifications and turn off email notifications for anything you already check in the CRM every day. Leave deal and mention alerts on.
blocks.confirmText: My profile and notifications are set — continue

blocks.html:
2. Email tracking: the step that does the most work

Linking your Outlook/Exchange mailbox lets Zoho read along. Emails to and from people in the CRM get attached to their records automatically — no BCC, no copy-paste, no “I’ll log it later.”

How to link it: gear icon (top right) → Channels → Email → select Office 365 / Exchange (IMAP) → authorize. Then check the two status lines:

  • Configuration Status: Working — the connection is live.
  • Sync Status: Completed — past mail has finished importing.

Sharing: leave Email Sharing set to Public — Shared with Everyone. That’s what lets a colleague pick up a deal without asking you for a recap.

Sending from a private account? Use your unique BCC to CRM address (found in these same settings) and that one email still lands on the record.

blocks.label: In Zoho CRM
blocks.instructions:
Go to gear icon → Channels → Email and read your Configuration Status and Sync Status. Write down what they say:
  • Both Working and Completed: you’re done here.
  • Anything else: don’t improvise. Note it and raise it with the Zoho admin — Christian or support@oneaccord.co.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve checked my email connection status — continue

blocks.html:
3. Your signature: the digital business card

Every email sent from Zoho should look like every other OneAccord email — same structure, same contact details.

  • Use the OneAccord brand standard. You may need to drop the photo to get under the size limit.
  • Include your Zoho Bookings link (built in Lesson 3). It turns “let’s find a time” into one click for the client.
  • Don’t have the template yet? Ask Abby — she manages the OneAccord signature templates.

blocks.label: In Zoho CRM
blocks.instructions: In Email Settings, open the Email Signature tab. Paste your standard OneAccord signature, remove the photo if Zoho rejects it for size, and save. Then send yourself a test email from inside Zoho and check how it looks on a phone.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve saved and tested my signature — continue

blocks.html:
4. The mobile app

Sales doesn’t only happen at a desk. The Zoho CRM app lets you check in at a client site, dictate a note straight after a call while it’s still fresh, and find an address without switching apps.

Two habits worth forming on day one: log the note before you leave the car park, and use check-in so your activity record matches where you actually were.

blocks.prompt: A colleague says they can’t see the emails you’ve been sending a shared prospect. Your mailbox shows Configuration Status Working. What’s the most likely cause?
options: You forgot to BCC the CRM address on each email
Your email sharing setting isn’t set to Public / Shared with Everyone
Your signature hasn’t been saved yet
blocks.feedbackCorrect: That’s the usual culprit. Tracking runs on the server side — BCC isn’t needed once the mailbox is linked — but if sharing is set to private, the emails are logged and only you can see them.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Check the sharing setting first: if Email Sharing isn’t Public / Shared with Everyone, emails are logged but stay visible only to you. BCC isn’t the issue once the mailbox is linked, and signatures and notifications don’t affect visibility.

blocks.promptHtml:
You’ve been working a prospect hard for two weeks: nine emails, two calls, one meeting. Your colleague opens the record to help you prepare for the next call and sees nothing — no emails, no notes, an empty activity list.

Walk through how you’d work out what’s wrong, in what order, and what you’d do about it. Include what you’d check in Zoho, and what you’d do about the two weeks already missing.
rubric: Checks the email connection first (Configuration Status and Sync Status under Channels → Email) rather than assuming the data is lost
Checks the sharing setting, since private sharing makes logged email invisible to others
Says how to catch up on the missing history — for example forwarding key emails using the BCC to CRM address, or logging the calls and meeting as activities
Escalates to the Zoho admin (Christian or support@oneaccord.co) rather than trying random fixes if the connection is broken
blocks.coachContext: Lesson on Zoho CRM personal setup. Correct diagnostic order: (1) Channels → Email configuration and sync status; (2) email sharing set to Public/Shared with Everyone; (3) whether the emails were sent from a mailbox other than the linked one (a private account needs the BCC to CRM address); (4) escalate to the Zoho admin. Past correspondence can be recovered by forwarding with BCC to CRM, and calls or meetings logged manually as activities. Notifications and signature settings do not affect logging. Zoho admin contacts: Christian or support@oneaccord.co.

blocks.promptHtml:
Different conditions. You’re emailing a prospect from your personal Gmail account on a Saturday, because that’s where you first swapped messages. On Monday you want that thread on the record — and you want the client-facing email to still look professional.

How do you handle it, and what would you change about how you work going forward?
rubric: Uses the BCC to CRM address so that specific thread lands on the record
Recognizes the professional-presentation problem of sending client email from a personal address and moves future correspondence into the work account
Keeps the signature and contact details consistent across both (the OneAccord standard)
Notes the effect on teammates — private-account email isn’t visible to colleagues unless it’s logged
blocks.coachContext: Transfer case for the same setup skills. Key points: the BCC to CRM address logs a single email sent from an outside account; the linked work mailbox logs automatically; email sharing should remain Public so colleagues can see correspondence; the OneAccord signature standard applies to anything a client reads; personal-account client email undermines presentation and continuity. Notifications have no bearing on logging.

blocks.label: Apply it in Zoho CRM
blocks.instructions:
Now finish your own setup using the five-point check. Any item you can’t tick, note it and raise it with the Zoho admin (Christian or support@oneaccord.co).
  1. Profile: photo, title, phone and time zone correct.
  2. Notifications: email duplicates off, deal and mention alerts on.
  3. Email: Configuration Status Working and Sync Status Completed; sharing set to Public.
  4. Signature: the OneAccord standard, tested by sending yourself an email.
  5. Mobile: the Zoho CRM app installed and signed in with your OneAccord credentials.
blocks.confirmText: I’ve run the five-point check on my own setup — continue
